summary: Stages 1–5 match skills/code-refiner.md line for line, and the receipt and scope-by-risk facts match AGENTS.md and docs/agents-detail.md. The weakest point is the join between re-verify and the receipt: no source says the code-refiner re-verify is the run that writes the receipt. Two true claims (the /audit worst-first ranking and the diff-economy definition) rest on skills/audit.md and skills/simplify.md, which are not in the spec's sources.

code.overview: Most of this flow is prose: the two reviewers, the merge of findings, the single fixer and the re-verify loop are all carried out by agents reading skills/code-refiner.md, skills/validate.md and skills/simplify.md. The code that exists is the deterministic part of the structural review (scripts/check-quality-mechanical.sh, run by .githooks/pre-commit and .github/workflows/quality.yml), a few shell tests that pin the wording of the skills, and the queue's per-task validate command. No code in the repo writes, reads or compares a verification receipt; CI simply runs everything on every pull request.

refs.anchor: collect() { while IFS= read -r f; do FILES+=("$f"); done < <(grep -E "$SOURCE_RE" || true); }
refs.title: File selection: explicit files, staged files, or the diff against main
refs.explain: collect reads file names from stdin and keeps those with a source extension (js, mjs, ts, tsx, sh, py, rb, go). With --staged the names come from the git index; with arguments the given files are used as is; with nothing they come from git diff main...HEAD. Each selected file is then passed to check_file.
refs.why: This is the same diff the flow gathers (git diff main...HEAD), but only for the mechanical check. The diff and file contents handed to the two reviewers are gathered by the agent, not by this script.

refs.anchor: emit "${file}:${MAX_LINES} [Readability/major] file is ${count} lines — exceeds ${MAX_LINES}-line limit; split into cohesive modules (or add a 'quality-ok: file-length — <reason>' pragma if it is one cohesive unit)"
refs.title: check_file: 500-line file length limit
refs.explain: Counts the lines in the file. If the count is over MAX_LINES (500) and the file has no 'quality-ok: file-length' pragma, it prints a Readability/major violation with a file:line citation and adds one to the violation count.
refs.why: Carries out the rubric's file-length criterion, which the structure reviewer may not override. Without it the limit would depend on a model noticing a long file.

refs.anchor: emit "${file}:${lineno} [Readability/minor] magic number — extract to a named constant (or use quality-ok: magic-number pragma if the value is self-documenting)"
refs.title: check_file: flag magic numbers
refs.explain: After the earlier skips (comments, named constants, test files, return/exit, pragma) and after quoted strings are stripped, the line is matched against a pattern for a bare integer of two or more digits. A match prints a Readability/minor violation with file:line. The pragma flag is then reset for the next line.
refs.why: Carries out the rubric's 'no magic numbers' criterion as a script, so the structure review's mechanical findings are repeatable.

refs.title: check_file: flag commented-out code
refs.explain: Reads the file again line by line. A line counts as commented code when it starts with // or # followed by a code keyword such as function, const, return or if. When two such lines are consecutive it prints a Clarity/minor violation for the second one.
refs.why: Carries out the rubric's 'no commented-out code' criterion. This one has no pragma, so the code must be deleted.

refs.anchor: check "persona preamble present"         "thoughtful senior engineer|joy to read|asks nothing unnecessary"
refs.title: Rubric format test: the four dimensions and scoring rules must be present
refs.explain: Each check greps lib/code-quality-rubric.md for one pattern and counts a pass or fail. This block requires the four dimension headings (Quality, Readability, Encapsulation, Clarity), the citation rule, the score formula, the weights, and the inline-override rules.
refs.why: The structure reviewer scores against this rubric file. The test stops the rubric from losing a dimension or its scoring rule; it does not check any score a reviewer gives.

refs.anchor: && ok "inline pragma awareness described" || fail "inline pragma awareness not described"
refs.title: simplify skill test: rubric include, score table, 10/10 gate
refs.explain: Greps skills/simplify.md for the include of the shared rubric, the 'Quality Scores' heading, the quality-override syntax, a description of inline pragmas, the 10/10 threshold and the auto-fix mode. Each grep records a pass or a fail.
refs.why: Pins the text the structure reviewer follows, including the 10/10 gate that re-verify depends on. It checks that the words exist, not that a review obeyed them.

refs.anchor: echo "pre-commit: ESLint configured but not installed — skipping (install deps, e.g. npm ci)" >&2
refs.title: pre-commit hook: lint and mechanical check on staged files
refs.explain: staged lists the staged files that match a pattern. If an ESLint config exists and ESLint is installed, the staged JS/TS files are linted. Then, if the mechanical check script exists, it runs with --staged. A non-zero exit from either step aborts the commit (set -eu).
refs.why: Any commit made after the fixer's pass goes through this hook when hooks are enabled, so the mechanical part of the structural check is re-run by code. The correctness re-check and the rubric scores are still done by an agent.

refs.title: Quality Gate workflow: mechanical checks on every pull request
refs.explain: On a pull request being opened or updated, the job checks out the code, lists every tracked source file, and runs the mechanical check on all of them. The job fails if the script reports any violation.
refs.why: This is the hosted backstop for the mechanical criteria: a violation the local review missed still blocks the PR. It checks all files, not just the diff.

refs.title: create-pr gate test: 10/10 threshold stated, gate placed before the PR body
refs.explain: Greps skills/create-pr.md for the 10/10 threshold and for the override mechanism. It then finds the line numbers of the 'Step 5' and 'Step 6' headings and fails unless Step 5 (the quality gate) comes first.
refs.why: Keeps the 10/10 rubric gate in the PR path and ahead of drafting the PR. It pins the order in the skill text only.

refs.anchor: /** Run a task's validation command; the worktree (if any) is the working dir. */
refs.title: runValidate: run a task's own validate command
refs.explain: Reads the task's validate command; with none it returns ok. Otherwise it runs the command with execSync in the task's worktree if it has one, else the current directory. On failure it returns the last three lines of the output.
refs.why: This is the 'task's own gates' part of the stage, for queued tasks. It always runs the command; it does not look for or write a receipt.

refs.title: queue done: a task completes only if its validate command passes
refs.explain: Finds the task. If it has a validate command and --skip-validate was not given, it runs the command without holding the queue lock, reloads the queue, and refuses to continue if the task changed meanwhile. If validation failed it records a failure, saves, and returns 1 without marking the task done.
refs.why: Makes 'done' depend on a check that just ran, which is the fail-closed idea of this stage. The check is re-run on every done; nothing is reused from an earlier run.

refs.title: CI verify job: the full test suite on every pull request to main
refs.explain: The job checks out the code, installs the Node version from .node-version, runs npm ci and then npm test. npm test runs the node tests, the tool tests, every scripts/test-*.sh and the repo checks.
refs.why: The flow says a missing receipt means checks re-run in full. There is no receipt lookup in this workflow, so that is what always happens here: hosted verification is never skipped or narrowed.

promptOnly.what: The agent runs git diff main...HEAD and reads each changed file in full to hand to the reviewers; only the mechanical check selects its own files by script.

The agent starts two fresh read-only subagents in one message, one applying skills/validate.md and one applying skills/simplify.md; the bug hunt, test-integrity check, rubric scores, diff economy and cross-file repeat check are all model judgment.

The invoking agent joins the two reports, makes findings on the same lines one item, orders correctness before structure, and either skips the fix when both are clean or presents the list and waits when run without --fix.
One agent applies the whole work list in a single pass, re-runs the repo's tests, and reports instead of editing when a fix would need a test changed.

The agent starts a fresh correctness and structural check on the new diff, loops the fix once on a regression, and stops with the remaining items if it still fails; only the mechanical criteria are re-checked by code.

No script writes, reads or compares a receipt keyed to tree identity, and none picks full suites versus affected checks; the rule exists only as text in AGENTS.md and docs/agents-detail.md, so the agent re-runs checks itself.
